Estimate what a run will cost

Source: R/cost.R
estimate_cost.Rd

estimate_cost() counts the calls that generate_synthetic() would make with the same arguments, guesses their tokens and multiplies them by the prices in sc_prices. estimate_interview_cost() does the same for cognitive_interview(). No model is called.

Usage

estimate_cost(
  instrument,
  models,
  personas = NULL,
  attempts = 1,
  respondents = 1,
  batch_size = 1,
  block_size = NULL,
  shuffle = FALSE,
  seed = 1,
  cache = sc_cache(),
  prices = sc_prices
)

estimate_interview_cost(
  instrument,
  models,
  personas = NULL,
  items = NULL,
  probes = sc_probes(),
  coder = NULL,
  pretest = NULL,
  interviews = 1,
  seed = 1,
  cache = sc_cache(),
  prices = sc_prices
)

Arguments

instrument

an sc_instrument().

models

one sc_model() or a list of them.

personas

an sc_personas() table, a character vector of descriptions, or NULL for respondents without a persona.

attempts

number of attempts per model.

respondents

number of respondents per persona in each attempt.

batch_size

number of respondents per call. The default, 1, keeps every respondent independent. A larger batch asks one call for several respondents of the same persona: That is cheaper, but the respondents in a batch may depend on each other (the model sees its own earlier answers), which can make them look more alike or more deliberately different than independent people would.

block_size

ask at most this many items per call. A respondent's blocks are asked one after another in the same conversation. NULL asks all items at once.

shuffle

shuffle the item order for each call?

seed

random seed for shuffling and for the mock provider. It is also part of the cache key: The same seed reuses saved answers, a new one asks the models again.

cache

the response cache: An sc_cache(), a folder, TRUE (the default folder) or FALSE (no cache). By default, saved answers are reused, so the same run twice gives the same data and the second run costs nothing. Use sc_cache(mode = "refresh") to ask again.

prices

the price table, sc_prices or your own with the same columns.

items

optional item names to interview about. NULL uses all items, or only the flagged items when pretest is given.

probes

the probes, from sc_probes().

coder

an sc_model() that codes the transcripts. NULL uses each respondent model to code its own interviews. The coder's temperature is set to 0 when it takes one.

pretest

optional result of synthetic_pretest(), or a data frame with an item column and an optional flag column (the reason, for example "low item-rest correlation"), or a vector of item names. Flagged items come first and get one extra probe.

interviews

number of interviews per model, persona and item.

Value

A tibble of class sc_cost with one row per model: model, provider, model_id, calls, cached (calls answered from the cache), input_tokens and output_tokens (of the calls still to make), input_price and output_price (dollars per million tokens), checked (the date of the price) and cost (dollars, NA when the model has no price). The attribute total holds the sum.

Details

Calls whose answers are in the response cache (see sc_cache()) are counted as free, since the run will not make them. Ollama and the mock provider are free too.

It is an estimate. Tokens are guessed from the length of the prompts (about four characters a token) plus the structured-output schema, and from the length of typical answers. Retries for invalid answers add to it. Reasoning models (such as gpt-5-nano) also bill their hidden reasoning as output, which the estimate leaves out. Treat the result as a guide to the size of the bill, and check the providers' prices for a large run.

See also

sc_prices, sc_cache(), generate_synthetic()

Examples

ins <- sc_instrument(hexaco_items, scale = c(1, 7))
per <- sc_persona_grid(age = c(25, 45, 65), template = "You are {age} years old.")
estimate_cost(ins, list(sc_model("anthropic"), sc_model("openai")), per,
              attempts = 5, respondents = 10, cache = FALSE)
#> Estimated cost: $0.23 for 300 calls.
#>  model            calls cached tokens_in tokens_out cost  prices_of 
#>  claude-haiku-5-5 150   0      535,050   144,750    $0.13 2026-11-03
#>  gpt-4.1-nano     150   0      487,050   144,750    $0.11 2026-02-18
#> An estimate: Tokens are guessed from the prompts, and retries add to it.
